chunks: One of his companions asked him about drinking in a single breath, so he said:
"If the one handing you the water is owned by you, then drink in three breaths; but if he is free, then drink it in a single breath."

key_terms.يُنَاوِلُكَ: hands to you or offers you

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about drinking water in one breath or three breaths?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses an etiquette related to drinking water and distinguishes between two social situations. It presents an instruction concerning how one should drink depending on whether the server is one's owned servant or a free person.
